researchQuestion: Can sample identity, instrument export, analysis sealing, and offline unblinding be made auditable without mistaking a file digest or signal similarity for proof that a new physical acquisition occurred?

identityContract.physicalSample: A registered persistent sample identifier may be used only for a physical sample. Synthetic fixtures use local MOCK-SAMPLE identifiers and must not resemble an issued IGSN.
identityContract.digitalObject: Each raw export and derived analysis receives its own digital-object identifier and SHA-256 digest; neither identifier is a physical-sample identifier.
identityContract.dualLabel: The machine-readable code and adjacent human-readable identifier must encode the same local sample or aliquot ID.

roleSeparation.preparer: Binds the physical label and aliquot parent but cannot open the arm map after commitment.
roleSeparation.acquisitionOperator: Runs the instrument and records the device receipt but cannot alter the arm map or analysis output.
roleSeparation.analyst: Receives sealed exports and cannot access the arm map before every analysis is sealed.
roleSeparation.independentCustodian: Commits the salted arm map offline and releases the salt and map once after all required exports and analyses are sealed.

commitment.canonicalForm: protocolId + newline + one-time random salt + newline + canonical JSON arm map
commitment.releaseGate: All required exports and analysis digests must be registered before key release.
commitment.warning: The repository uses a disclosed deterministic demonstration salt only for reproducibility. It is not a reusable secret and cannot qualify physical custody.

receiptClasses.synthetic-emulator: Tests software interfaces only and can never establish a site or physical acquisition.
receiptClasses.independent-witness: A named institutional witness attests start, stop, label, and export; acceptance still depends on local policy.
receiptClasses.device-signed: A verified signature binds device identity, monotonic counter, acquisition interval, label, and export digest.

threeEvidenceLayers.byteIdentity: A raw-byte digest detects exact byte reuse or alteration but changes under harmless re-encoding.
threeEvidenceLayers.semanticContent: A canonical numeric digest catches syntax-only re-encoding; a tolerant signal fingerprint may quarantine regridded or scaled near-copies but cannot prove copying.
threeEvidenceLayers.physicalOccurrence: Only acquisition-side evidence independent of file contents can support a claim that a new measurement occurred. Content-only evidence is insufficient in indistinguishable worlds.

verdicts.accept-interface: The synthetic event and evidence contract is internally consistent; no physical claim follows.
verdicts.reject: A deterministic contract violation is present.
verdicts.quarantine: Content is suspicious but also compatible with a legitimate repeat; independent acquisition evidence is required.
verdicts.unverified-physical: The event chain is syntactically valid but lacks an accepted acquisition-side attestation.

siteReadinessGates.criterion: Physical labels and scanner output reconcile at the site; issued persistent IDs, if used, resolve to the same physical samples.
A real instrument export contains complete time, counter, device, sample, and processing provenance fields.
An independent person or service holds and releases the one-time arm-map key after sealing.
A device signature or institutional witness independently binds the acquisition event to the exported bytes.
Institutional EHS, radiation, ventilation, waste, instrument, and supply gates from INTERVENTION-PILOT-0.2 are satisfied.

independenceRule: Development signals, deterministic salts, emulator receipts, and mutation fixtures must not be reused to adjudicate a physical pilot. A site qualification requires separately generated labels, exports, keys, receipts, and reviewers.
